description: Spacing token definitions, irregularity audit across all components, and resolved application rules. All components must reference token names — never raw pixel values.

baseline.description: The 4px-base scale. All spacing in the system must use one of these tokens.

tokens.usage: Micro spacing — icon gaps, dot separators, tight inline elements
Small spacing — internal component gaps, label margins, table cell padding
Close spacing — between tightly related elements, badge padding, chip gaps
Default inline spacing — icon-text gap in horizontal cards, form row gaps
Component padding — card padding all sides, card grid gap default, hero meta gap
Generous spacing — modal padding, page horizontal padding, section dividers
Section spacing — padding-top between page sections, hero vertical padding
Page-level spacing — page bottom padding, large layout gaps

baseline.note: sp-5 (20px), sp-7 (28px), sp-10 (40px), sp-14 (56px) do not exist in the scale. Values in those ranges must be snapped to the nearest defined token.

irregularitiesAudit.description: All off-scale values found across buttons, cards, modals, tables, and the article layout. Each entry documents where the value was found, why it is irregular, and the resolution.

items.issue: Between sp-1 (4px) and sp-2 (8px). Not on scale.
items.resolution: Spec-defined exception. Button vertical padding is a fixed spec value from buttons.json and must not be changed to maintain the prescribed pill shape. Document as a component exception — not a spacing token.

items.issue: Between sp-6 (24px) and sp-8 (32px). Not on scale.
items.resolution: Spec-defined exception. Button horizontal padding is a fixed spec value from buttons.json. Document as a component exception.

items.foundIn: Metric delta — inline gap between arrow and text
items.issue: Between sp-1 (4px) and sp-2 (8px). Not on scale.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-1 (4px). The difference is imperceptible and alignment improves with a token value.

items.foundIn: Hero meta — gap between meta items; Section label — margin-bottom
items.issue: Between sp-1 (4px) and sp-2 (8px). Used inconsistently — sometimes 6px, sometimes 8px for visually equivalent contexts.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-1 (4px) for decorative micro-gaps (dot separators). Snap to sp-2 (8px) for text-adjacent label margins. Eliminate 6px entirely.
items.snapTo: sp-1 or sp-2 depending on context
items.rule: Use sp-1 (4px) for decorative gaps and dot separators. Use sp-2 (8px) for label-to-content margins.

items.foundIn: Card title — margin-bottom before body text; Button row — gap between buttons inside a card
items.issue: Between sp-2 (8px) and sp-3 (12px). Used in multiple components inconsistently.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-2 (8px) for tight internal component spacing. Snap to sp-3 (12px) where slightly more breathing room is needed between distinct content elements.
items.rule: Use sp-2 (8px) for intra-element gaps (title to body). Use sp-3 (12px) for between-element gaps (body to buttons).

items.foundIn: Section labels, legend items, chart tick labels — used widely as a 'small label' size
items.issue: Not on the type scale. Caption token is 12px / weight 300. Using 11px creates an undocumented sub-caption tier.
items.resolution: All instances of 11px font-size must use the caption token (12px / weight 300) instead. Eliminates the undocumented size.

items.foundIn: Metric delta text — font-size between caption (12px) and body-sm (14px)
items.issue: Not on the type scale. Creates an undocumented intermediate size.
items.resolution: Snap to caption token (12px) for supplementary metric annotations, or body-sm (14px) if it needs to read as data. Eliminate 13px entirely.
items.rule: Use caption (12px) for metric annotations and supporting labels. Use body-sm (14px) for metric values that are data-adjacent.

items.foundIn: Card grid gap — defined minimum (min 14px, max 32px)
items.issue: Between sp-3 (12px) and sp-4 (16px). The defined minimum is off-scale.
items.resolution: Snap minimum card gap to sp-3 (12px). Maximum remains sp-8 (32px). Default stays sp-6 (24px).

items.foundIn: Hero title — margin-bottom; Section title — margin-bottom before content
items.issue: Between sp-4 (16px) and sp-6 (24px). Not on scale. Used as a mid-point that doesn't exist in the token system.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-4 (16px) for title-to-body margins within a section header block. Use sp-6 (24px) when more separation is needed between the header block and the first content element.
items.rule: Use sp-4 (16px) for heading-to-body margins. Use sp-6 (24px) for heading-block-to-content separation.

items.issue: Between sp-12 (48px) and sp-16 (64px). Not on scale.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-12 (48px). The 2px difference is imperceptible and alignment with the token scale improves predictability.

items.issue: Between sp-12 (48px) and sp-16 (64px). Not on scale.
items.resolution: Snap to sp-12 (48px) for hero vertical padding. Use sp-16 (64px) only for the largest layout containers where maximum visual separation is needed.

resolvedApplicationRules.description: Token-to-context mapping for every spacing use case across the design system. All values resolved to scale.

fontSizeAudit.description: Font sizes found outside the type scale. All must be replaced with the nearest type scale token.

items.foundIn: Section labels, legend items, chart tick labels
items.issue: Not on type scale — sits below caption (12px)
items.resolution: Use caption token (12px / Roboto 300). Imperceptible visual difference; brings all labels on scale.

items.foundIn: Metric delta text, some annotation labels
items.issue: Not on type scale — between caption (12px) and body-sm (14px)
items.resolution: Use caption (12px) for purely supplementary annotations. Use body-sm (14px) if the value is data-facing and needs to read clearly.
items.snapTo: caption or body-sm depending on context

do: Always reference a spacing token — never raw pixel values in component styles
Use sp-1 (4px) for micro-gaps: icon-text inline gaps, dot separators, badge internal padding
Use sp-2 (8px) for intra-component spacing: title-to-body, label margins, table cell padding
Use sp-3 (12px) for close but distinct elements: button group gaps, card body-to-button gap
Use sp-4 (16px) for default inline layout gaps: icon-to-content in horizontal cards, heading-to-body
Use sp-6 (24px) for component padding: card padding, card grid gap, chart panel padding
Use sp-8 (32px) for generous separation: modal padding, page horizontal padding, table header gap
Use sp-12 (48px) for section-level spacing: section padding-top, hero vertical padding
Use sp-16 (64px) for page-level spacing: page bottom padding, maximum layout gaps
Treat button padding (7px vertical, 25px horizontal) as spec-defined component exceptions — never replace with scale tokens
dont: Do not use 5px, 6px, 7px (except button exception), 10px, 11px, 13px, 14px, 20px, 25px (except button exception), 50px, or 56px as spacing values
Do not introduce new spacing values outside the 8-token scale
Do not use 11px or 13px as font sizes — use caption (12px) or body-sm (14px) from the type scale
Do not use sp-12 (48px) where sp-8 (32px) is sufficient — prefer the smaller token unless visual separation genuinely requires more
Do not apply sp-16 (64px) inside components — it is a page-level token only
